- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2 points below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting — anticipate upward correction 2–3 days ahead.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse — forecast should gently slope upward toward prior mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — dampen volatility in forecast unless sentiment is strongly sustained.
